26| class VideoLoader():
27|     """Implementation of VideoLoader.
28| 
29|     The VideoLoader is a wrapper around the torchvision video interface. With
30|     the VideoLoader you can read specific frames or the next frames of a video.
31|     It automatically switches to the `video_loader` backend if available. Reading
32|     sequential frames is significantly faster since it uses the VideoReader 
33|     class from torchvision.
34| 
35|     The video loader automatically detects if you read out subsequent frames and
36|     will use the fast read method if possible. 
37| 
38|     Attributes:
39|         path:
40|             Root directory path.
41|         timestamps:
42|             Function that loads file at path.
43|         backend:
44|             Tuple of allowed extensions.
45|         transform:
46|             Function that takes a PIL image and returns transformed version
47|         target_transform:
48|             As transform but for targets
49|         is_valid_file:
50|             Used to check corrupt files
51| 
52|     Examples:
53|         >>> from torchvision import io
54|         >>>
55|         >>> # get timestamps
56|         >>> ts, fps = io.read_video_timestamps('myvideo.mp4', pts_unit = 'sec')
57|         >>>
58|         >>> # create a VideoLoader
59|         >>> video_loader = VideoLoader('myvideo.mp4', ts)
60|         >>>
61|         >>> # get frame at specific timestamp
62|         >>> frame = video_loader.read_frame(ts[21])
63|         >>>
64|         >>> # get next frame
65|         >>> frame = video_loader.read_frame()
66|     """
67|     def __init__(self, path: str, timestamps: List[float], backend: str = 'video_reader'):
68|         self.path = path
69|         self.timestamps = timestamps
70|         self.current_timestamp_idx = 0
71|         self.last_timestamp_idx = 0
72|         self.pts_unit='sec'
73|         self.backend = backend
74| 
75|         has_video_reader = io._HAS_VIDEO_OPT and hasattr(io, 'VideoReader')
76| 
77|         if has_video_reader and self.backend == 'video_reader':
78|             self.reader = io.VideoReader(path = self.path)
79|         else:
80|             self.reader = None
81|     
82|     def read_frame(self, timestamp = None):
83|         """Reads the next frame or from timestamp.
84| 
85|         If no timestamp is provided this method just returns the next frame from
86|         the video. This is significantly (up to 10x) faster if the `video_loader` 
87|         backend is available. If a timestamp is provided we first have to seek
88|         to the right position and then load the frame.
89|         
90|         Args:
91|             timestamp: Specific timestamp of frame in seconds or None (default: None)
92| 
93|         Returns:
94|             A PIL Image
95| 
96|         """
97|         if timestamp is not None:
98|             self.current_timestamp_idx = self.timestamps.index(timestamp)
99|         else:
100|             # no timestamp provided -> set current timestamp index to next frame
101|             if self.current_timestamp_idx < len(self.timestamps):
102|                 self.current_timestamp_idx += 1
103| 
104|         if self.reader:
105|             if timestamp is not None:
106|                 # Calling seek is slow. If we read next frame we can skip it!
107|                 if self.timestamps.index(timestamp) != self.last_timestamp_idx + 1:
108|                     self.reader.seek(timestamp)
109| 
110|             # make sure we have the tensor in correct shape (we want H x W x C)
111|             frame = next(self.reader)['data'].permute(1,2,0)
112|             self.last_timestamp_idx = self.current_timestamp_idx
113| 
114|         else: # fallback on pyav
115|             if timestamp is None:
116|                 # read next frame if no timestamp is provided
117|                 timestamp = self.timestamps[self.current_timestamp_idx]
118|             frame, _, _ = io.read_video(self.path,
119|                                         start_pts=timestamp,
120|                                         end_pts=timestamp,
121|                                         pts_unit=self.pts_unit)    
122|             self.last_timestamp_idx = self.timestamps.index(timestamp)    
123|         
124|         
125|         if len(frame.shape) < 3:
126|             raise ValueError('Unexpected error during loading of frame')
127| 
128|         # sometimes torchvision returns multiple frames for one timestamp (bug?)
129|         if len(frame.shape) > 3 and frame.shape[0] > 1:
130|             frame = frame[0]
131| 
132|         # make sure we return a H x W x C tensor and not (1 x H x W x C)
133|         if len(frame.shape) == 4:
134|             frame = frame.squeeze()
135| 
136|         # convert to PIL image
137|         image = Image.fromarray(frame.numpy())
138|         return image

140| def _make_dataset(directory,
141|                   extensions=None,
142|                   is_valid_file=None,
143|                   pts_unit='sec'):
144|     """Returns a list of all video files, timestamps, and offsets.
145| 
146|     Args:
147|         directory:
148|             Root directory path (should not contain subdirectories).
149|         extensions:
150|             Tuple of valid extensions.
151|         is_valid_file:
152|             Used to find valid files.
153|         pts_unit:
154|             Unit of the timestamps.
155| 
156|     Returns:
157|         A list of video files, timestamps, frame offsets, and fps.
158| 
159|     """
160| 
161|     # handle is_valid_file and extensions the same way torchvision handles them:
162|     # https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/_modules/torchvision/datasets/folder.html#ImageFolder
163|     both_none = extensions is None and is_valid_file is None
164|     both_something = extensions is not None and is_valid_file is not None
165|     if both_none or both_something:
166|         raise ValueError('Both extensions and is_valid_file cannot be None or '
167|                          'not None at the same time')
168| 
169|     # use filename to find valid files
170|     if extensions is not None:
171|         def _is_valid_file(filename):
172|             return filename.lower().endswith(extensions)
173| 
174|     # overwrite function to find valid files
175|     if is_valid_file is not None:
176|         _is_valid_file = is_valid_file
177| 
178|     # find all instances (no subdirectories)
179|     instances = []
180|     for fname in os.listdir(directory):
181| 
182|         # skip invalid files
183|         if not _is_valid_file(fname):
184|             continue
185| 
186|         # keep track of valid files
187|         path = os.path.join(directory, fname)
188|         instances.append(path)
189| 
190|     # get timestamps
191|     timestamps, fpss = [], []
192|     for instance in instances:
193| 
194|         if AV_AVAILABLE and torchvision.get_video_backend() == 'pyav':
195|             # This is a hacky solution to estimate the timestamps.
196|             # When using the video_reader this approach fails because the 
197|             # estimated timestamps are not correct.
198|             with av.open(instance) as av_video:
199|                 stream = av_video.streams.video[0]
200|                 duration = stream.duration * stream.time_base
201|                 fps = stream.base_rate
202|                 n_frames = int(int(duration) * fps)
203| 
204|             timestamps.append([Fraction(i, fps) for i in range(n_frames)])
205|             fpss.append(fps)
206|         else:
207|             ts, fps = io.read_video_timestamps(instance, pts_unit=pts_unit)
208|             timestamps.append(ts)
209|             fpss.append(fps)
210| 
211| 
212|     # get frame offsets
213|     offsets = [len(ts) for ts in timestamps]
214|     offsets = [0] + offsets[:-1]
215|     for i in range(1, len(offsets)):
216|         offsets[i] = offsets[i-1] + offsets[i] # cumsum
217| 
218|     return instances, timestamps, offsets, fpss

221| class VideoDataset(datasets.VisionDataset):
222|     """Implementation of a video dataset.
223| 
224|     The VideoDataset allows random reads from a video file without extracting
225|     all frames beforehand. This is more storage efficient but is slower.
226| 
227|     Attributes:
228|         root:
229|             Root directory path.
230|         extensions:
231|             Tuple of allowed extensions.
232|         transform:
233|             Function that takes a PIL image and returns transformed version
234|         target_transform:
235|             As transform but for targets
236|         is_valid_file:
237|             Used to check corrupt files
238| 
239|     """
240| 
241|     def __init__(self,
242|                  root,
243|                  extensions=None,
244|                  transform=None,
245|                  target_transform=None,
246|                  is_valid_file=None):
247|         
248|         super(VideoDataset, self).__init__(root,
249|                                            transform=transform,
250|                                            target_transform=target_transform)
251| 
252|         videos, video_timestamps, offsets, fps = _make_dataset(
253|             self.root, extensions, is_valid_file)
254|         
255|         if len(videos) == 0:
256|             msg = 'Found 0 videos in folder: {}\n'.format(self.root)
257|             if extensions is not None:
258|                 msg += 'Supported extensions are: {}'.format(
259|                     ','.join(extensions))
260|             raise RuntimeError(msg)
261| 
262|         self.extensions = extensions
263| 
264|         backend = torchvision.get_video_backend()
265|         self.video_loaders = \
266|             [VideoLoader(video, timestamps, backend=backend) for video, timestamps in zip(videos, video_timestamps)]
267| 
268|         self.videos = videos
269|         self.video_timestamps = video_timestamps
270|         # offsets[i] indicates the index of the first frame of the i-th video.
271|         # e.g. for two videos of length 10 and 20, the offsets will be [0, 10].
272|         self.offsets = offsets
273|         self.fps = fps
274| 
275|     def __getitem__(self, index):
276|         """Returns item at index.
277| 
278|         Finds the video of the frame at index with the help of the frame 
279|         offsets. Then, loads the frame from the video, applies the transforms,
280|         and returns the frame along with the index of the video (as target).
281| 
282|         For example, if there are two videos with 10 and 20 frames respectively
283|         in the input directory:
284| 
285|         Requesting the 5th sample returns the 5th frame from the first video and
286|         the target indicates the index of the source video which is 0.
287|         >>> dataset[5]
288|         >>> > <PIL Image>, 0
289| 
290|         Requesting the 20th sample returns the 10th frame from the second video
291|         and the target indicates the index of the source video which is 1.
292|         >>> dataset[20]
293|         >>> > <PIL Image>, 1
294| 
295|         Args:
296|             index:
297|                 Index of the sample to retrieve.
298| 
299|         Returns:
300|             A tuple (sample, target) where target indicates the video index.
301| 
302|         Raises:
303|             IndexError if index is out of bounds.
304| 
305|         """
306|         if index < 0 or index >= self.__len__():
307|             raise IndexError(f'Index {index} is out of bounds for VideoDataset'
308|                              f' of size {self.__len__()}.')
309| 
310|         # each sample belongs to a video, to load the sample at index, we need
311|         # to find the video to which the sample belongs and then read the frame
312|         # from this video on the disk.
313|         i = len(self.offsets) - 1
314|         while (self.offsets[i] > index):
315|             i = i - 1
316| 
317|         # find and return the frame as PIL image
318|         timestamp_idx = index - self.offsets[i]
319|         frame_timestamp = self.video_timestamps[i][timestamp_idx]
320|         sample = self.video_loaders[i].read_frame(frame_timestamp)
321| 
322|         target = i
323|         if self.transform is not None:
324|             sample = self.transform(sample)
325|         if self.target_transform is not None:
326|             target = self.target_transform(target)
327| 
328|         return sample, target
329| 
330|     def __len__(self):
331|         """Returns the number of samples (frames) in the dataset.
332| 
333|         """
334|         return sum((len(ts) for ts in self.video_timestamps))
335| 
336|     def get_filename(self, index):
337|         """Returns a filename for the frame at index.
338| 
339|         The filename is created from the video filename, the frame number, and
340|         the video format. The frame number will be zero padded to make sure 
341|         all filenames have the same length and can easily be sorted.
342|         E.g. when retrieving a sample from the video
343|         `my_video.mp4` at frame 153, the filename will be:
344| 
345|         >>> my_video-153-mp4.png
346|     
347|         Args:
348|             index:
349|                 Index of the frame to retrieve.
350| 
351|         Returns:
352|             The filename of the frame as described above.
353|                 
354|         """
355|         if index < 0 or index >= self.__len__():

139| 
140|         Args:
141|             dataset:
142|                 PyTorch/torchvision dataset.
143|             transform:
144|                 Image transforms (as in torchvision).
145|             index_to_filename:
146|                 Function which takes the dataset and index as input and returns
147|                 the filename of the file at the index. If None, uses default.
148|

151|

153|         >>> # load cifar10 from torchvision
154|         >>> import torchvision
155|         >>> import lightly.data as data
156|         >>> base = torchvision.datasets.CIFAR10(root='./')
157|         >>> dataset = data.LightlyDataset.from_torch_dataset(base)
158| 
159|         """

161|         dataset_obj = cls(
162|             None,
163|             transform=transform,

165|         )

167|         # populate it with the torch dataset

174|         Args:
175|             index:
176|                 Index of the queried item.
177| 
178|         Returns:
179|             The image, target, and filename of the item at index.
180| 
181|         """
182|         fname = self.index_to_filename(self.dataset, index)
183|         sample, target = self.dataset.__getitem__(index)

185|         return sample, target, fname

201|         """Returns all filenames in the dataset.
202| 
203|         """
204|         list_of_filenames = []
205|         for index in range(len(self)):
206|             fname = self.index_to_filename(self.dataset, index)
207|             list_of_filenames.append(fname)

211|              output_dir: str,
